creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster msg post --to <pane>` exited 1, "nobody here or on a machine linked to this one is called <pane>", for a devenv pane whose agent had joined as `src`. `muster docs msg` says `--to` takes a pane name even if its agent "need not have joined anything", and that a pane nobody here goes by is looked for on linked machines.

## Measured: 2026-10-01, laptop to devenv

A laptop agent ended a Claude Code session in a devenv pane, resumed the same session in the same pane, and then tried to report back to it. `--to <pane>` and `--to <pane>@devenv` were both refused. The devenv daemon was connected, and `muster window` showed the pane running claude. `--group <me>+src@devenv` worked and woke the same agent, which had kept its participant name `src` across the resume.

Inferred, not checked: a pane name stops resolving once a participant holds the pane, at least from another machine.

## Things that might be true

- **Resolve `--to <pane>` to whichever participant is in that pane**, on this machine or a linked one.
- Failing that, have the refusal name the participant: "<pane> is src@devenv".
title: 📨 msg post --to <pane> is refused once a participant holds the pane
